institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location and area of study at the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some welcome days - unfortunately it was not clear where to go as an English speaker.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't too hard! I fortunately knew student who lived in Vienna the previous year. My suggestion is to speak with other students who have gone on Erasmus!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's important to participate in social activities with the university so you can make new friends. Living off campus can be lonely if you don't interact with others.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses at BOKU tend to overlap. It was very challenging to find courses that didn't overlap.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to pay your registration fee and show up in person to receive your BOKU card. Once you have your card you can sign up for courses in BOKUonline.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can consult your study plan or ask questions to other students (including students in the OH) or you can speak with student services.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not very successful in registering for courses I wanted. You have to take ~10-12 classes to reach 30 ECTS. Many classes overlap in time and subject matter. I had mandatory classes that prevented me from taking courses that I was genuinely interested in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have lots of patience and speak with other BOKU students about the courses before you sign up. Also, you will have to skip classes but you will be okay in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses at BOKU vary in difficulty.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The host university had more lectures and less interactive study. At BOKU there is a more formal relationship between student and professor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to take field trip courses because they are more interactive.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had a blood test that was not reimbursed by my insurance. I also elected to get the FMSE vaccination which was not covered by insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Red peppers were more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wish there were more opportunities for students who do not speak German.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports activities were available. The Erasmus network also offered various opportunities to experience the culture. Vienna also hosts lots of festivals and cultural events in the Summer semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I suggest yoga - Yoga Kula was very nice and offered courses in English.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get the Klimaticket so you can travel all of Austria! The Rax mountains are nice for hiking and not too far from Vienna. It is beautiful to visit Salzburg in December (Stadtalm Naturfreundehaus was a lovely hostel).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend events and don't be shy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The relationship between student and professor was very different. I also found the older generation in Vienna to be less welcoming than people in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the BOKU ball and the museums.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you really would like to go to BOKU then be prepared for juggling classes
2. Learn some German before going in order to make exploring easier
3. Have patience and expect paperwork

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the location of Vienna and explore when you have a chance.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and learning about Austria.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to taking 11 courses was an absolute pain. Also, the language barrier was difficult at times. At one point, a sports course was listed in English online so I attended the orientation and the instructor only spoke in German even though two of us were not German speakers.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
